title: An icon exported as a picture can come out with nothing behind it too
goal: Export an icon you drew on a blank canvas as a PNG and the white canvas is baked into every pixel behind it, with nothing in the sheet to say otherwise. SVG now lets you leave the canvas out; a picture should too, so an icon handed over as a PNG can sit on a coloured page or a dark theme.
notes: Falls out of an-icon-exported-as-svg-comes-out-with-nothing-b (2026-09-16), which fixed SVG only. Reproduced the same day: PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1 Scripts/playtest.sh /tmp/tmp-png-bg-walk.json --no-build wrote icon-as-png.png (900x700, hasAlpha yes) from a pen-drawn shape on a blank 900x700 canvas, and reading it back gave top-left (5,5) r255 g255 b255 a255 and bottom-right (895,695) r255 g255 b255 a255: opaque white, not empty. The SVG side is SVGExport.Background plus SVGExport.backdrop(in:flatImages:) in PhotonzCore, and ExportDialog.backgroundRow already holds the control and already knows the backdrop for the target (it reads FlatBitmap.colors once per sheet). The picture path is EditorState.exportComposite plus ExportSizer; the smallest version is to render with the backdrop layer set isVisible = false. JPEG and HEIC hold no transparency, so the row must not appear for them.
acceptance: Exporting an icon drawn on a blank canvas as PNG can produce a file that is see-through behind the shapes
The same Include the background control appears for PNG, in the same place it appears for SVG, and is not offered for a format that cannot hold transparency
Exporting a screenshot or a whole screen still carries its background, unasked
A walk writes the picture and proves the corner pixels are empty
